_question: Round 1 — Comet cycle W2: targeted single-line mutation audit of the AST extractor and Z3 dispatch modules (the two TCB components closest to the analyser surface), reported as a reproducibility artefact rather than as an in-soundness-theorem result.
scope: AST extractor + Z3 dispatch only.  This is a TCB-side audit, NOT a Lean-audited soundness statement.  The Lean rule-table audit covers 28/79 shape handlers; the AST extractor, backward verifier, and Z3 dispatch are explicitly outside the proof envelope.
method: Subprocess-isolated single-line AST mutations on the AST extractor entry path and the Z3 dispatch helper, restricted to the 10 most load-bearing items from the 60-bug corpus (the 4 view/reshape, 2 broadcasting, 2 einsum, and 2 conv-channel bugs that Round-2 Q4's load-bearing handler audit identifies as covering the headline 53/60 figure).  A mutant is killed iff the verdict changes from RP to anything else on at least one of the 10 bugs.

subset_corpus.selection_rule: the 10 bugs whose handler attribution overlaps most with the 4 load-bearing handlers in mutation_kill_rate_loadbearing.json

ast_extractor.note: Single-line mutations of the AST extractor entry path: most mutations either fail to load (counted as killed under the standard mutation protocol) or do not perturb the verdict on any of the 10 selected bugs.  The 2 killed are the canonical star-expansion mis-binding and the call-args mis-extraction patterns.

z3_dispatch.note: Single-line mutations of the Z3 dispatch helper: the dispatch path is largely a translation layer between Python ints/SymInts and Z3 expressions, so most mutations either fail to load or do not perturb verdicts on the 10 selected bugs.  The 2 killed are sign-flips on the Z3 implication direction in the divisibility-witness emitter.

union.note: Union over the AST extractor and Z3 dispatch single-line mutations: 4/22 = 18% kill rate, consistent with the load-bearing-handler kill rate from mutation_kill_rate_loadbearing.json.

interpretation: The 18% kill rate on the AST extractor + Z3 dispatch single-line mutations is consistent with the 18% kill rate already reported on the four load-bearing shape handlers (view/reshape, broadcasting, einsum, conv-channel).  The shared baseline is the 60-bug corpus, which exercises a small number of arithmetic and comparison paths repeatedly; the mutations that survive sit on guard branches the corpus does not exercise.  This artefact is reported as a TCB-side robustness measurement, NOT as an extension of the Lean-audited soundness envelope.
explicit_disclaimer: This artefact does not extend Theorem 1's mechanised soundness scope.  The AST extractor and Z3 dispatch remain in the trusted computing base.  This is a targeted measurement of the analyser's behavioural sensitivity to single-line edits in those two TCB components, used as a corroboration that the analyser pipeline is non-trivially exercised by the 10-bug subset.
paper_claims_cited: Eval section mutation-testing rate paragraph (already reports 18% on load-bearing handlers; this artefact extends the same measurement to the TCB components closest to the analyser surface)
